summary: The exact candidate reconciles implicit per-worker admission with enabled decode graph coverage. The original numeric default changes from 4096 on base to 32, preventing default admission above the captured ceiling while retaining explicit overrides with a warning.

tests.what_was_measured: Original failure reproduced meaningfully: issue inputs resolve to 4096 rather than 32. The candidate-only warning-helper case also fails with AttributeError; four unaffected cases pass.
All 6 submitted policy and warning regressions pass against checked-out candidate source.
50 tests and 7 subtests pass, including independent graph-limit, low-token, disabled/absent-graph, explicit-override, and DP-local boundaries plus adjacent pool configuration.

gpu_execution_evidence: The host exposes one AMD Instinct MI350X under ROCm 7.2, not the reported NVIDIA L40. Tests were deterministic source-level CPU tests; no GPU result is claimed.
remaining_limitations: The reported NVIDIA L40/Qwen2.5-0.5B/ShareGPT latency transition and its 4x magnitude were not rerun because the prepared host is AMD gfx950 and the model/workload assets were unavailable.
The review verifies that default admission can no longer exceed configured decode graph coverage; it does not benchmark the admission-queue TTFT tradeoff on the reported architecture.
Explicit max-running-requests values above graph coverage intentionally remain possible and warn; this is outside the no-flags default failure contract.
